record.name: Ethiopia
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. The Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute leads AI research and policy implementation. The national policy assigns developer licensing and AI product and service certification; the cited policy and official accounts do not establish a role for the institute in evaluating the safety of advanced models.

related_bodies.name: Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute (EAII)
related_bodies.role: Its remit covers research, development and policy implementation. The national policy also assigns developer licensing and certification of domestic and imported AI products and services. It is an autonomous federal AI institute accountable to the Prime Minister under regulation 510/2022. No qualifying role in evaluating the safety of advanced models was identified.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. No qualifying institute for the safety of advanced models was established by the English searches or the primary regulation/UNESCO account. The Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute has broad research, deployment, policy, authorisation and imported-technology certification powers. Those clauses are a real evaluation-adjacent signal, but do not specify technical evaluation of advanced general-purpose model capabilities or severe risks. check.language_note: The recorded am queries use a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. The earlier English-search pass on 17 October 2026 left the then-recorded national or official-language coverage unchanged; the work is described below. The additional status review searched Amharic and English and read the bilingual national policy; other Ethiopian languages were not exhaustively searched. Search batches for the additional status review, using 1-based positions in check.searches: 4, 5; 6. Each group records the same exact registered URLs found in its combined search results, without attribution to an individual query. Explicit page opens and finds and unverified URL variants are excluded. Groups list the recorded queries; some requests also contained additional queries retained in the research evidence.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The UNESCO readiness assessment was produced with national authorities. Independence from the government statutory institute account was not substantiated. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.
check.governance_note: Medium confidence rests on the retrieved government policy text hosted by Law Ethiopia, a mirrored primary source, and the recorded Amharic and English searches. The policy distinguishes EAII's product and service certification from monitoring policy implementation. The establishing regulation is also held as a mirror; UNESCO provides supporting governance context. The official Finance Ministry account describes dedicated AI institutions and development priorities, without setting out an evaluation mandate. No official-host copy of the policy or establishing regulation was retrieved in the partial check. This remains a bounded negative finding, not proof of absence.

record.notes:
The national AI policy was read in Amharic and English. It assigns the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute policy coordination, developer licensing and certification of domestic and imported AI products and services. Its monitoring and evaluation provisions concern policy implementation. These provisions do not establish a role evaluating capabilities or behaviour risks of advanced models. Later official material, including the Finance Ministry's 15 October 2026 account of AI institutions and development priorities, did not identify a superseding designation or institute proposal. This is a bounded search finding, not a finding that such work cannot exist.

The policy text supporting medium confidence was retrieved from Law Ethiopia, not an official government host. The regulation is also a mirrored primary text. The official Finance Ministry account supports the institutional context but does not supply the detailed mandate. An attempt to obtain an official-host legal text failed; medium confidence therefore retains this access limitation.

next_check.reason: Check future EAII regulations or technical mandates for evaluation of the safety of advanced models; current reviewed powers concern certification and policy coordination.
